Question: What are the best tricks to keep yourself motivated?
Answer: Say you want to study. You can study. You want to start. But instead, you open YouTube. You want to watch just one video so that you can study intensely. It becomes a chain. You watch one video, then the other, and you end up wasting two hours on YouTube. Now you don't feel like studying at all. I'm not saying motivation is bullshit. It's great. But it is hardly needed when we start the work. It is needed we're tired. When we want to slog. When we feel like giving up after giving it a good start. Starting isn't hard. You just need to put your tushy on the chair. The real drag is perseverance. To become consistent at something. Don't take motivation before doing the work. Consume motivation in between. Take it to persevere. Take it when your legs are worn out and you don't feel like walking anymore. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: I love you. Can you love me?
Answer: Say there's a writer. He writes fictional answers with ease. He's exceptionally good with words. He sometimes posts his photos alongside the answers. He looks good. He respects people in the comments section. He's humble, down-to-earth, and charming. His inbox is filled with praises and confessions. He has a secret link attached to his profile where he has received a few messages which blew his mind. For example, this: He's flattered. He gets elated when he reads such messages. But he can't understand how on earth can someone fall for a person, online. Just by his words. Do you really think it's practical to fall in love with someone whom you don't even know? He might be terrible in person. His profile might be handled by someone else. Maybe someone else is writing for him. Is writing good enough to fall in love with someone? For me, no. It shouldn't be. You should fall in love with a live fresh and blood. You should fall in love with his voice, gestures, laugh, or maybe, just maybe how protective his touch is. You can admire someone online. You can get attracted to someone online. You might have a big, big crush on someone online. But unless you talk to him, in person, are you sure that this feeling is love? P.S. The person who has texted this, probably we can meet. Not as a date. Maybe we can meet normally, talking about life and death and books and writing? We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Do we need friends in life?
Answer: One of my roompartners left permanently for Hyderabad yesterday. It's been a strange void after that. He was my chai partner. We talked about books. And he used to come back at around 6 PM and we discussed his day at work. I went to have tea in the evening. I was sitting there, alone, when this angel came near me. I started patting it. It sat down. I think it could sense my void. I caressed it for a couple of minutes until my chai was finished. Then I stood up. I made the payment and left straightaway. It was looking at me. Maybe it wanted to me sit more. But I had to go. I had to read a book. It didn't follow me. Dogs can be great friends sometimes. A friend who can sense what's going on inside your mind. We all are gifted, Shubham KP
